[LUNI.5.2.1] **A `label` is display only. It creates no way to write the
unit.** Only the canonical name and explicit `alias` entries reach the
symbol table; a `label` is the string rendered by the `u` format
specifier ([LUNI.11.2]) and nothing else.

The two are easy to confuse because a label usually *looks* like a symbol —
`label "grad"`, `label "frac"` — and a reader of a unit library reasonably
assumes a short form printed beside a unit is one they may type. It is not.
A unit whose label is not also an alias advertises a spelling the compiler
will reject as an unknown unit.

So the rule for an author declaring a unit: **if the short form should be
writable, it is an `alias`; a `label` is for the reader of output.** Where
both are wanted, declare both — they are independent clauses of the same
declaration ([LUNI.4.3]) and naming the same string twice is correct, not
redundant.
